items.title: Pay 'processing fee' to supposedly release energy refund (likely scam — do not pay)
items.quote: Damit wir sie auszahlen können, überweisen Sie bitte die einmalige Bearbeitungsgebühr von 49,90 € bis zum 27.11.2026 auf das Konto IBAN CY17 0020 0128 0000 0012 0052 7600.
items.computation: The letter prints a fixed calendar date for the payment: 'bis zum 27.11.2026'. No period calculation is needed since this is an explicit date. 27 November 2026 is a Friday, not a weekend or public holiday in NRW, so no adjustment applies. However, this demand bears all hallmarks of an advance-fee refund scam (unsolicited large refund, upfront fee required, foreign IBAN, urgency threat that the claim 'verfällt endgültig'), so the obligation itself is almost certainly fraudulent and should not be paid.

warnings: This letter shows the classic pattern of an advance-fee refund scam: an unexpectedly large 'refund' (612,00 €) is dangled, but a smaller upfront 'processing fee' (49,90 €) must be paid first before any money is released — legitimate refunds never require the recipient to pay a fee first.

The payment is requested to a Cypriot IBAN (CY17 ...) for what claims to be a German energy-cost refund matter; a foreign bank account for a domestic consumer refund is a strong red flag and should never be used.

The sender 'Verbraucher-Rückerstattungsstelle Energie' with an address in Nicosia, Cyprus is not a known or official German consumer-protection or energy-regulation body; real German energy refunds are handled directly by the person's own energy supplier or grid operator, not by a third-party 'refund office'.
The letter uses pressure/urgency language ('Verstreicht die Frist, verfällt Ihr Anspruch endgültig') to rush the recipient into paying quickly without checking — a typical fraud tactic.
Recommend not transferring any money, not replying with personal/bank details, and reporting this letter as a suspected scam (e.g. to the Verbraucherzentrale or police) rather than acting on it.
